analysis.rationale: R1 re-analysis confirms R0 and finds no candidate that matches better. New evidence: (1) the apparent 'global tone step' (mean_shift<0, variance_ratio<1, asymmetric highlight roll-off measured in flat regions: identity below clean~150 then -3.8 @192, -12.3 @222, -25.1 @248, -28.6 @254) is fully reproduced by speckle:3 -> JPEG:2 through multiplicative-noise clipping at 255 plus JPEG smoothing, with a flat-region curve match within 0.4 levels at every bin; no x_distortion global function (brightness shift/gamma, contrast scale/stretch, saturation, quantization) can produce an asymmetric highlight-only shoulder, so no global step is warranted. (2) dct_zero_ratio is a strong overlooked discriminator: target 0.5587 vs JPEG-only-on-clean 0.7278 (diff 0.169) vs speckle:3+JPEG:2 0.5588 (diff 0.0001), proving noise precedes JPEG and fixing the JPEG severity. (3) step2's GAUSSIAN_YCrCb verdict is a JPEG/gamma-suspect false positive (cross_ch 0.79-0.94 from JPEG YCbCr operations + shared clipping; residual_intensity_corr 0.25-0.57 from the |residual|-vs-intensity relation of the clip shoulder). (4) peeled extreme_pct 62.8-65% is a 'res<=0' convention FP (residual=target-sim, mean shift -7 makes about half of all pixels count as extreme; zero_ratio only 0.072). (5) pair4 chroma ratio 1.2423 is content-dependent (pairs range 0.89-1.24), no consistent saturation step. (6) blur ruled out again (spectral_slope_ratio 0.969-0.995, anisotropy 0). All 5 pairwise candidates that alter the noise type/severity or JPEG severity either fail a signal check or break the continuous global fingerprint (speckle2+jpeg1 bb 8.3%; speckle4+jpeg2 sigma 40% + ms -9.12/vr 0.812; gaussian_RGB3+jpeg2 ms -2.26/vr 0.899; YCrCb3+jpeg2 sigma 40%; speckle3+jpeg3 bb 16.1%/dct 0.6445). Decision NO_CHANGE; verdict kept UNCERTAIN per SKILL (noise step can never be LIKELY; PSNR>=40dB unreachable under noise).
